newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down on U.S. led profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down on U.S. led profit-taking.

text.p: IPE December Brent crude ended lower on Wednesday following a U.S.-led profit-taking selloff.

December Brent finished down 18 cents at $23.81 a barrel, off a high of $24.48. Contracts fell sharply on NYMEX, where prices were sent reeling after failing to break resistance at new post Gulf War highs posted this week.
Thinly-traded November Brent last traded up 12 cents at its expiry at $24.85 a barrel.
Dealers said heating oil markets in particular had suffered a case of the jitters on Wednesday after the meteoric price rise which has crude up 40 percent in four months.
Markets shrugged off apparently bullish inventory data with APIs showing a fall in U.S. northeast distillate stocks.
"It's not the first time that bullish APIs have given us a bearish market," a trader said. "They just couldn't sustain it."
In Europe physical heating oil premiums lost some lustre as a fleet of cargoes from the U.S. made its weight felt.
Diesel cargoes in northwest Europe were bid at a huge $15 a tonne below easier offers.
"The market's got a severe case of the jitters here," said an IPE broker. "People seem to be questioning whether this market should be quite as high as it is."
IPE gas oil ended down $3 a tonne at $227.50, or $7.50 off its highs for the day.
The gas oil-Brent crack spread shrank below $6 for the first time in several weeks to end at $5.90 for December contracts.
